headline: Passenger-led growth, margin-accretive propulsion ahead.

highlights: Gross margins improved by 256 bps YoY (+227 bps QoQ) to 28.7% in Q2FY27, supported by a richer mix from higher passenger rail system contribution and price variation clauses protecting project-level realizations.
EBITDA stood at INR 1,069mn (+27.9% YoY/+12.7% QoQ), above our estimates of INR 936mn.
EBITDA margin improved by 303bps YoY (+109 bps QoQ) to 13.5% in Q2FY27, supported by operating leverage from the passenger ramp and lower drag from freight volumes.
PAT stood at INR 632mn (+70.7% YoY/+20.2% QoQ), above our estimates of INR 560mn.
valuation: The Mumbai Line 5 and Line 6 prototypes are slated for Q4FY27E, Bangalore is nearing completion, Gujarat deliveries are underway, and the Pune aluminium line is targeting the first fully India-made aluminium coach in Q1-Q2FY28E, building a differentiated capability aligned with the eventual shift to aluminium-based high-speed rolling stock under the government's seven- corridor plan.

The larger margin lever is propulsion: from BHEL- supplied units in the current 1,280-car contract (plus 30% option), Titagarh targets prototype in FY27E, limited series by FY28E and full production by FY30E.
Outlook & Valuation: Titagarh Rail Systems enters H2FY27 with a structurally stronger revenue mix and improved visibility across both segments.
watch: Key Highlights Structural mix shift toward Passenger Rail with visible growth runway: Titagarh is transitioning from a freight-led franchise to a balanced passenger-plus-freight platform.

Freight stabilization and de-risked execution: The Indian Railways option quantity order restores wagon visibility for 3-4 quarters and into FY28E, underpinning a return to ~1,000 wagons per month by Q4FY27E and supporting a ~INR 286.95bn order book.
